text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German debt, surprising even bullish traders, cleared several key resistance levels in Wednesday trading, as soft German economic data and the U.S. Treasury market' early gains paved the way for hefty profits. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.11, up 0.32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilt futures ended lower amid confusion over Italy's possible involvement in the first stage of European monetary union. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-1/32, down 9/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - PARIS, Feb 5 (Reuter) - French bond futures finished MATIF trading higher at 131.00 in a session supported by firm T-Bonds ahead of news from the U.S. FOMC monetary policy council and helped back in Europe by a drop in German industry orders. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 131.00, up 0.34 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to higher levels in late afternoon trade after shrugging off a report of a plan for Italy to delay its EMU entry beyond 1999 while taking some support from the stronger lira. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.43, up 0.71 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened unchanged on Wednesday, as market participants awaited the outcome of a Federal Reserve monetary policy meeting. The market widely anticipates that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy-making arm of the Fed, will leave interest rates unchanged. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-1/32, down 6/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.73 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended the Tokyo session higher but well off its intraday high. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.25, unchanged from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The dollar Eurobond sector remained subdued as players waited for an announcement from the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. No interest rate changes were expected, analysts said, and the announcement was due around 1915 GMT.
